q: A test is 99% accurate, and 1 person in 1,000 has the disease. You test positive. About how likely is it that you have the disease?
why: Out of 100,000 people: 100 are sick and 99 test positive. 99,900 are well and 999 of them test positive by mistake. So 99/1098 ≈ 9%.
Myth. P(clouds | rain) is close to 1, but P(rain | clouds) is much lower.
Only for independent events. In general P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B | A).

q: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.1. Find P(A | B).
why: Divide by the event you're given, B: P(A | B) = 0.1/0.4 = 0.25.

q: Why does a low base rate matter for a medical test?
o: False positives from the large healthy group outnumber the true positives
It makes the test less accurate
It makes the test more sensitive
why: Even a small error rate, applied to a huge healthy group, gives many false alarms.
